rv.q: In the long, exhausting reality show formerly known as life, which cannot be traversed with the aid of TiVo, there are peaks and there are valleys. Qualifying as traditional high points are weddings and children’s birthdays, career triumphs, the day you bought those jeans that actually flatter.

That “Spelling Bee” has succeeded not only in maintaining but even amplifying its spontaneity despite the increased commercial stakes of a Broadway move reflects the freshness of this big-hearted little show.
Here there was the possibility of something meaningful, which has been treated as a cartoon.

cn.t: Critics are largely charmed by this modest musical about misfit spellers, praising its warmth and intact Off-Broadway appeal, though one dissenter finds it precious and lacking bite.

vs.sum: Broadway's only thrust-stage theater offers an unmatched intimate experience — no seat is more than a few rows from the action. Sightlines are excellent from every angle, though some seats face actors' backs during certain scenes.

acc.note: Elevator accessible through adjoining building. Loop technology and neck induction systems available.
